questions.stem:
Given that the binomial expansion, in ascending powers of $x$, of
$6(4+Ax)^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
is $B-\frac{1}{4}x+Cx^2+...$

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) find the values of the constants $A$, $B$ and $C$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: For $B=6\times4^{-\frac{1}{2}}=3$ which may be implied by their expansion.
M1: Attempts to find $A$ condoning the omission of their "3". Look for $-\frac{1}{2}\times(\frac{Ax}{m})=-\frac{1}{4}x$ oe leading to a value for $A$.
A1: $A=\frac{2}{3}$ or an exact equivalent.
M1: Attempt to find $C$ condoning the omission of their "3". Look for $\frac{(-\frac{1}{2})\times(-\frac{3}{2})}{2}\times(\frac{A}{m})^2=...$ leading to a value for $C$.
A1: $C=\frac{1}{32}$ oe e.g. $0.03125$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Must be consistent with their $...\left(1+\frac{A}{m}x\right)^{-\frac12}$ but condone the omission of the "3". Note the omission of the "3" (if correct) leads to A = 2.
- A1: $A=\frac23$ or an exact equivalent or e.g. $0.\dot6$. Allow if seen embedded in $6(4+Ax)^{-\frac12}$
- M1: or $\frac{(-\frac12)\times(-\frac32)}{2}\times\left(\frac{Ax}{m}\right)^2=...$ oe with their numerical value of A leading to a value for C. Must be consistent with their $...\left(1+\frac{A}{m}x\right)^{-\frac12}$ where m could be 1. Note the omission of the "3" (if correct) with a correct A leads to C = $\frac{1}{96}$.
- A1: $C=\frac{1}{32}$ Allow if seen embedded in their expansion.

parts.mark_scheme:

parts.label: c

In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.

parts.label: i
parts.text:
(i) The volume, $V$, of a spherical balloon is increasing at a constant rate of $70\pi\,\text{cm}^3\text{s}^{-1}$
Find the rate of increase of the radius of the balloon, in $\text{cm}\,\text{s}^{-1}$, at the instant when the radius of the balloon is 5 cm.
[The volume $V$ of a sphere of radius $r$ is given by the formula $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3$]
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: States or uses $\frac{dV}{dt}=70\pi$ oe.
B1: States or uses $\frac{dV}{dr}=4\pi r^2$ oe.
M1: Attempts to use $\frac{dV}{dt}=\frac{dV}{dr}\times\frac{dr}{dt}$ or equivalent with $r=5$ and their $\frac{dV}{dr}$ and $\frac{dV}{dt}$ correctly placed, e.g. $70\pi = 4\pi\times5^2\times\frac{dr}{dt}$.
A1: $\left(\frac{dr}{dt}\right)=0.7$ oe e.g. $\frac{7}{10}$ (Units are not required but if given must be correct).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- Alternative: $V=70\pi t$ B1; $\frac43\pi r^3=70\pi t$ B1; $\frac43\pi r^3=70\pi t\Rightarrow4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}=70\pi\Rightarrow100\frac{dr}{dt}=70$ or $r^3=\frac{105}{2}t\Rightarrow r=\left(\frac{105}{2}t\right)^{\frac13}$, $\frac{500}{3}t=70\Rightarrow t=\frac{50}{21}$, $\Rightarrow\frac{dr}{dt}=\frac13\left(\frac{105}{2}\right)^{\frac13}\left(\frac{50}{21}\right)^{-\frac23}$ M1; $\frac{dr}{dt}=0.7$ A1. M1: For either: Differentiating $\frac43\pi r^3=70\pi t$ to obtain $...r^2\frac{dr}{dt}=...$ and substituting r = 5 or Making r the subject to obtain $r=...t^{\frac13}$ and then differentiating to obtain $\frac{dr}{dt}=...t^{-\frac23}$ and then substituting t obtained from $\frac43\pi(5)^3=70\pi t$. A1: 0.7 oe (Units are not required but if any are given they must be correct)
- B1: oe e.g. $\frac{dt}{dV}=\frac{1}{70\pi}$. B1: oe e.g. $\frac{dr}{dV}=\frac{1}{4\pi r^2}$ which may be seen as $\frac{dV}{dr}=100\pi$ or $\frac{dr}{dV}=\frac{1}{100\pi}$ if r = 5 has been substituted.

parts.label: ii
parts.text:
(ii) The depth of water in a cave is being monitored.
The rate of increase in the depth of water, $h$ cm, at a particular point in the cave is modelled by the differential equation
$\frac{dh}{dt}=\frac{k}{h^3}$
where $k$ is a constant and $t$ hours is the time after monitoring began.
Given that
• initially the depth of water was 4 cm
• 5 hours after monitoring began, the depth of water was 6 cm
• $T$ hours after monitoring began, the depth of water was 10 cm
solve the differential equation to find the value of $T$.
Give your answer to one decimal place.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Separates variables and integrates both sides to obtain $...h^4=kt(+c)$ or equivalent (no constant of integration needed for this mark).
A1: $\frac{1}{4}h^4=kt(+c)$ or equivalent, with or without a constant of integration.
M1: Requires a constant of integration and using $t=0,h=4$ to find $c$ (leads to $c=64$). Condone poor integration and poor rearrangement for this mark.
dM1: Uses $t=5,h=6$ to find $k$ (dependent on previous mark), leading to $k=52$. Condone poor integration and poor rearrangement.
ddM1: Dependent upon all three previous M's. For substituting $h=10$ into their equation and finding $T$ (or $t$).
A1: Awrt 46.8 or exact e.g. $\frac{609}{13}$, $\frac{9744}{208}$. Allow better accuracy e.g. 46.85. Units not required but if given must be correct.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- dM1: It is dependent upon the previous mark and having two correctly placed constants. A1: It does not have to be referenced as "T" so just look for the correct value.
- Alternative using definite integration: $\left[\frac14h^4\right]_4^6=[kt]_0^5$, $324-64=5k\Rightarrow k=52$, $\left[\frac14h^4\right]_4^{10}=[52t]_0^T\Rightarrow2436=52T\Rightarrow T=46.8$. M1, A1 as main scheme. M1: Attempts $\left[\frac14h^4\right]_4^6=\frac14\times6^4-\frac14\times4^4=260$ Condone poor integration of $h^3$. dM1: Attempts $[kt]_0^5=5k$ and solves $\left[\frac14h^4\right]_4^6=[kt]_0^5$ to find k. It is dependent upon the previous mark. dddM1: Dependent upon all three previous M's. It is for attempting $\left[\frac14h^4\right]_4^{10}=[52t]_0^T$ to find T (or t). A1: Awrt 46.8 or exact e.g. $\frac{609}{13}$, $\frac{9744}{208}$.
- Alternative when k is placed differently: $\int\frac{h^3}{k}dh=\int dt\Rightarrow\frac{h^4}{4k}=t+c$; $\frac{64}{k}=c$, $\frac{324}{k}=5+c\Rightarrow c=\frac{16}{13}, k=52$; $\frac{10^4}{208}=t+\frac{16}{13}\Rightarrow T=\frac{609}{13}$. M1: obtain $...\frac{h^4}{k}=t(+c)$. A1: $\frac{h^4}{4k}=t(+c)$. M1: Requires a constant of integration and using either $t=0,h=4$ or $t=5,h=6$ to obtain an equation connecting c and k. Condone poor integration for this mark. dM1: Uses both $t=0,h=4$ and $t=5,h=6$ to obtain 2 equations connecting c and k and solves simultaneously to obtain a value for c and a value for k. You do not need to be concerned how they solve their equations as long as they obtain a value for c and a value for k. It is dependent upon the previous mark and having two correctly placed constants. dddM1: Dependent upon all three previous M's. It is for substituting h = 10 into their equation and finding T (or t). A1: Awrt 46.8 or exact.

questions.stem:
Given that $n\in\mathbb{N}$, use algebra to prove by contradiction that
"if $n^2 - 4n + 5$ is even then $n$ is odd"
(4)

parts.text:
Given that $n\in\mathbb{N}$, use algebra to prove by contradiction that
"if $n^2 - 4n + 5$ is even then $n$ is odd"
(4)
parts.mark_scheme:
B1: Sets up a suitable assumption in words: e.g. (Assume) "$n^2-4n+5$ is even and $n$ is even".
M1: Uses algebra with $n=2k$ or equivalent and attempts $n^2-4n+5$.
A1: $4k^2-8k+5$ (oe for their $n$).
A1*: Completes proof with (i) a correct expression that is clearly odd, e.g. $4(k^2-2k)+5$ or $2(2k^2-4k+2)+1$ or $(2k-2)^2+1$, (ii) an acceptable statement with reason that it is odd, and (iii) a minimal conclusion e.g. "Hence contradiction", "so proven". Note that B0M1A1A1 is not possible.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- If the same variable is used e.g. n = 2n allow all but the final mark for otherwise correct work. But allow n = 2N as a different variable.
- B1: Look for e.g. $n^2-4n+5$ is even and n is even or e.g. if n even then $n^2-4n+5$ is even. The word "assume" is not required but there must be a statement referring to $n^2-4n+5$ is even and n is even. Condone e.g. "if $n^2-4n+5$ is even then n is even".
- M1: e.g. $n=2k+2$ or e.g. $n=4k$. A1: or equivalent for their n such as $4(k^2-2k)+5$ or e.g. $4k^2+1$ for $n=2k+2$. A1*: or e.g. $4(k^2-2k+1)+1$. Condone $4k^2-8k+5=even-even+odd=odd$
- Note that attempts that consider a contradiction such as e.g. (Assume) "$n^2-4n+5$ is odd and n is odd" score no marks.
- "$n^2-4n+5$ is even and n is even" $n^2-4n+5=(n-2)^2+1$ is even so $(n-2)^2$ must be odd. If $(n-2)^2$ is odd then $(2k-2)^2$ is odd (as n is even) hence contradiction. So if $n^2-4n+5$ is even then n is odd. Mark such attempts as follows: B1: As main scheme M1: Completes the square on $n^2-4n+5$ to obtain $(n-2)^2+...$ or uses $n^2-4n+5=n(n-4)+...$ A1: $n^2-4n+5=(n-2)^2+1$ or e.g. $n^2-4n+5=n(n-4)+5$ A1: Fully reasoned and convincing argument with a (minimal) conclusion. If you are unsure if a particular response deserves merit then use review.

questions.stem:
In this question you must show all stages of your working.
Solutions relying entirely on calculator technology are not acceptable.
Figure 2 shows a sketch of the curve $C$ with parametric equations
$x = 2\cos2t$ $y = \sin^3t$ $-\frac{\pi}{2}<t<\frac{\pi}{2}$
where $t$ is a parameter.
The point $P$ lies on $C$ where $t=\frac{\pi}{6}$
The line $l$, shown in Figure 2, is the tangent to $C$ at $P$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Use parametric differentiation to show that
(i) $\frac{dy}{dx}=k\sin t$ where $k$ is a constant to be found
(ii) an equation for $l$ is $3x+16y-5=0$
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
(i) M1A1: $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{dy/dt}{dx/dt}=\frac{3\sin^2t\cos t}{-4\sin2t}$.
A1: $\frac{3\sin^2t\cos t}{-4\sin2t}=\frac{3\sin^2t\cos t}{-8\sin t\cos t}=-\frac{3}{8}\sin t$ (or equivalent working using $\sin2t=2\sin t\cos t$).
(ii) B1: $t=\frac{\pi}{6}\Rightarrow x=1, y=\frac{1}{8}$.
M1: $m=-\frac{3}{8}\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right)=-\frac{3}{16}\Rightarrow y-\frac{1}{8}=-\frac{3}{16}(x-1)$.
A1*: $3x+16y-5=0$ (cso, must follow correct M1A1 in part (i)).
Official notes (completeness pass):
- (a)(i) M1: Condone incorrect attempts on $\frac{dy}{dt}$ and $\frac{dx}{dt}$. Note that x and/or y may have been adapted before differentiation. A1: Correct $\frac{dy}{dx}$ in any form from correct work. A1: from fully correct work so must follow M1A1 so M1A0A1 is not possible. You may need to check the working carefully as the value of k can be deduced from the given tangent equation. e.g. $3x+16y-5=0\Rightarrow m=-\frac{3}{16}$, $m=k\sin\frac{\pi}{6}\Rightarrow k=-\frac38$
- (a)(ii) M1: Correct method for tangent. It is awarded for: substituting $t=\frac{\pi}{6}$ into their $k\sin t$ or their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ to find m; using $y-y_1=m(x-x_1)$ where $x_1$ and $y_1$ are their values of x and y when $t=\frac{\pi}{6}$ or using $y=mx+c$ with their values and proceeds to c = ... A1*: Proceeds with a correct method and correct work to the given answer with sufficient working. if $-\frac38\sin t$ has been obtained fortuitously or from incorrect work in part (i), this mark should be withheld.

parts.label: b
parts.text:
The line $l$ intersects the curve $C$ again at the point $Q$.
(b) Using algebra and showing detailed reasoning, find the exact coordinates of $Q$.
(6)
parts.mark_scheme:
M1: Substitutes $x=2\cos2t$ and $y=\sin^3t$ into $3x+16y-5=0$: $3(2\cos2t)+16(\sin^3t)-5=0$.
dM1: Uses $\cos2t=\pm1\pm2\sin^2t$ or equivalent: $6(1-2\sin^2t)+16\sin^3t-5=0$.
A1: Correct cubic equation with terms collected: $16\sin^3t-12\sin^2t+1=0$.
ddM1: Solves cubic equation via any appropriate means to obtain $\sin t=\alpha$ where $|\alpha|<1$ and $\alpha\neq\frac{1}{2}$: $(2\sin t-1)^2(4\sin t+1)=0\Rightarrow\sin t=-\frac{1}{4}$.
dddM1: Substitutes their $\sin t=-\frac{1}{4}$ into both $x=2\cos2t$ and $y=\sin^3t$ to obtain values for $x$ and $y$.
A1: $Q\left(\frac{7}{4}, -\frac{1}{64}\right)$. Allow any equivalent exact values and allow as $x=..., y=...$.
Official notes (completeness pass):
- M1: Condone slips as long as the intention is clear. dM1: The equivalent work could be e.g. $6\cos2t=6(\cos^2t-\sin^2t)=6(1-\sin^2t-\sin^2t)$ etc. A1: The "= 0" may be implied by later work e.g. by their attempt to solve. ddM1: including via a calculator. dddM1: This may be using appropriate identities for finding x or via a calculator e.g. $x=2\cos\left(2\sin^{-1}\left(-\frac14\right)\right)$
- Note that it is possible to answer (b) by eliminating t: 1. Via x: $\sin^2t=\frac{2-x}{4}\Rightarrow y=\left(\frac{2-x}{4}\right)^{\frac32}$, $4(2-x)^3=(5-3x)^2\Rightarrow4x^3-15x^2+18x-7=0\Rightarrow x=\frac74\Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{64}$. Score as: M1: Uses the x coordinate and $\cos2t=\pm1\pm2\sin^2t$ or equivalent work to find an equation connecting $\sin t$ and x e.g. $\sin^2t=\frac{2-x}{4}$ and uses this to find y in terms of x. dM1: Substitutes their y in terms of x into $3x+16y-5=0$ to obtain an equation in terms of x only. A1: Correct cubic equation with terms collected and all on one side e.g. $4x^3-15x^2+18x-7=0$. The "= 0" may be implied by later work. ddM1: Solves cubic equation via any appropriate means including via a calculator to obtain a value for x where $x\neq1$. dddM1: Uses their value of x in $3x+16y-5=0$ to find a value of y. A1: $Q\left(\frac74,-\frac{1}{64}\right)$ Allow any equivalent exact values and allow as x = …, y = …
- 2. Via y: $\sin t=y^{\frac13}$, $x=2-4y^{\frac23}$, $12y^{\frac23}=16y+1\Rightarrow1728y^2=(16y+1)^3\Rightarrow4096y^3-960y^2+48y+1=0\Rightarrow y=-\frac{1}{64}\Rightarrow x=\frac74$. Score as: M1: Uses the y coordinate to find an equation connecting $\sin t$ and y e.g. $\sin t=y^{\frac13}$ and uses this to find x in terms of y. dM1: Substitutes their x in terms of y into $3x+16y-5=0$ to obtain an equation in terms of y only. A1: Correct cubic equation e.g. $4096y^3-960y^2+48y+1=0$. ddM1: Solves cubic equation ... to obtain a value for y where $y\neq\frac18$. dddM1: Uses their value of y in $3x+16y-5=0$ to find a value of x. A1: $Q\left(\frac74,-\frac{1}{64}\right)$
- Note that some candidates are bypassing the cubic and clearly using the "solve" function on their calculator. This is not satisfying the rubric of the question or the rubric on the front of the question paper. These will be marked as special cases. e.g. $3x+16\left(\frac{2-x}{4}\right)^{\frac32}-5=0\Rightarrow x=\frac74$ Scores SC M1M1A0M0M1A1; $3x+16\sin^3\left(\frac12\arccos\frac{x}{2}\right)-5=0\Rightarrow x=\frac74$ Scores SC M1M0A0M0M1A1. In such cases award marks as follows: M1: Uses the x coordinate and $\cos2t=\pm1\pm2\sin^2t$ or equivalent work to find an equation connecting $\sin t$ and x and uses this to find y in terms of x. dM1: Substitutes their y in terms of x into $3x+16y-5=0$ to obtain an equation in terms of x only that is algebraic i.e. does not involve inverse trig functions. A0: Not available M0: Not available M1: Uses their value of x in $3x+16y-5=0$ to find a value of y. A1: $Q\left(\frac74,-\frac{1}{64}\right)$
